claims.claim_text: A nontrivial binary upcycle exists with n=12,d=3,L=512; it answers Question 9.2 affirmatively.
claims.basis: Accepted full-scope claim and proof; fresh execution of displayed verifier and literal wildcard expansion.

claims.claim_text: The 512 windows partition all 4096 binary 12-words into sets of eight completions.
claims.basis: Fresh count array:4096 entries, all1;512 starts with8 completions each.

claims.claim_text: 128 octal digits specify the complete cycle.
claims.basis: Four32-digit rows, Python literal, and frozen witness agree.

claims.claim_text: The window length 12 does not divide cycle length 512.
claims.basis: Integer arithmetic:512 modulo12 is8.

claims.claim_text: Chen, Kitaev, Mütze and Sun introduced universal partial words and cyclic versions.
claims.basis: CKMS17 original PDF p1 abstract,p2 Section1.2 and arXiv abstract explicitly address introduction and cyclic forms.

claims.claim_text: Fillmore et al. Theorem 3.1 gives binary n=8,d=1 examples.
claims.basis: FGKMM26 Theorem3.1 and its displayed examples; each displayed block has one wildcard in8 positions.

claims.claim_text: Fillmore et al. Question 9.2 asks whether upcycles with d>1 exist.
claims.basis: FGKMM26 Section9 Question9.2; same immutable source question.

claims.claim_text: Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2 multiply alphabet size while preserving n,d.
claims.basis: FGKMM26 Theorem5.1 and Corollary5.2 retain n,d while enlarging alphabet.

claims.claim_text: Corollary 8.14 requires d=n/4 for nontrivial period-four frames.
claims.basis: FGKMM26 Corollary8.14, specialize frame period m=4; hypotheses nontrivial and period4 retained.

claims.claim_text: Carey et al. Definition 8.2 permits several cyclic words in a universal partial quasi-family.
claims.basis: CKKP25 Definition8.2 permits a set of cyclic partial words with unique joint coverage.

claims.claim_text: The four displayed rows have 128 octal digits and decode to the accepted word.
claims.basis: All printed rows and verifier literal match frozen word.txt after decoding.

claims.claim_text: Digits 0,1,7 decode to wildcard000, wildcard001, wildcard111.
claims.basis: Three-bit binary expansion of0,1,7 checked directly.

claims.claim_text: Completion sets are disjoint iff ordinary unequal symbols occur at a common offset.
claims.basis: Both implications of the printed lemma checked from coordinate compatibility; consistent specified bits produce a common completion.

claims.claim_text: The cycle has 512 positions with wildcards precisely at indices zero modulo four, also cyclically.
claims.basis: 128 length4 blocks; literal word check gives wildcard iff index mod4=0, and4 divides512.

claims.claim_text: Every window has three wildcards and nine ordinary symbols, with no repeated physical position.
claims.basis: All512 literal12-windows checked; each has3 wildcards,9 ordinary positions;12<512 prevents repeated indices.

claims.claim_text: Each completion set has exactly eight members.
claims.basis: Three distinct wildcard offsets have2^3=8 independent completions.

claims.claim_text: All 130816 pairs have an ordinary conflict; every test succeeds.
claims.basis: Source and PDF-extracted verifier both execute all130816 pairs successfully.

claims.claim_text: Pairwise disjoint completion sets have union cardinality 512*8=4096=2^12.
claims.basis: Lemma plus disjoint finite union and exact cardinalities512*8=4096=2^12.

claims.claim_text: The direct loop checks all 4096 total words at all 512 starts without sampling.
claims.basis: Read loops and reran exact program from source and extracted PDF; literal expansion corroborates.

claims.claim_text: Eleven starts 501 through 511 wrap around and are included.
claims.basis: Start500 ends511 without wrapping; starts501..511 wrap and range512 includes all11.

claims.claim_text: The program performs 2097152 compatibility tests and prints the stated counts.
claims.basis: 4096*512=2097152 and recorded actual output matches.

claims.claim_text: The direct check counts starting indices, with shared characters read from one decoded word and exact integer counts.
claims.basis: Read program:one window per start,characters read from same u;sum traverses all windows using Python integers.

claims.claim_text: FGKMM26 raises n not dividing cycle length immediately after Question 9.2.
claims.basis: FGKMM26 paragraph immediately following Question9.2 discusses n not dividing a^(n-d).
